To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) for the static system, the optimal decision to accept a request depends only on the bandwidth requirements of the request and the requests that have arrived earlier; (b) the optimal decision for the dynamic system is similar, but the bandwidth requirement of the current request is replaced with the maximum of its bandwidth requirement and that of the requests that have already been scheduled; and (c) the optimal decision is difficult to compute for the dynamic system and the heuristic algorithm performs well.

(1) the optimal scheduling algorithm is to accept all requests that have arrived by the current time, if possible, and (2) the performance of a system with delayed scheduling decisions can be improved by using an adaptive algorithm that adjusts the delay parameter as a function of time

(1) for a system that can accommodate any bandwidth requirement, delaying scheduling decisions can improve the system's performance, (2) the improvement is significant for systems where bandwidth requirements can only assume a few discrete values, and (3) the performance improvement decreases with an increase in the number of bandwidth requirements that the system can accommodate
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a framework for the analysis and design of a channel reservation service.
the design of an optimal reservation system.
the performance evaluation and modeling of reservation systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of a reservation system with delayed scheduling decision is superior to a system with immediate scheduling decision.
delaying the decision to schedule the requests can be beneficial to the performance of the system.
the performance of the reservation service is improved when decisions are delayed, and the improvement in performance is more significant as the bandwidth requirement of a request increases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of the reservation service with delayed decisions is comparable to that of the immediate decision system, while the complexity of the algorithms is much less.
, if users are willing to accept a delay in scheduling decisions, a significant performance improvement may be achieved.
, for the system under consideration, the benefits of delaying scheduling decisions are not significant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under certain conditions, a system can improve its performance by delaying the scheduling decisions.
, under certain conditions, a system can achieve significant performance improvement with only a modest increase in delay.
delaying the decision-making process can improve system performance significantly.
